title: 31.4 A 91.25% Peak Power-Conversion-Efficiency Capacitive Power-Management IC Supporting up to 5.68mJ Burst Energy Delivery Using a Single External Capacitor for mm-Scale IoT Applications
problem: mm-scale IoT devices with solid-state batteries face peak-power-delivery bottleneck due to high internal battery resistance (200Ω+), limiting burst energy to 4.8μJ, insufficient for peak transient loads (mW-level). Conventional approaches either use large storage capacitors (2% energy extraction) or on-chip capacitors (limited density at 0.87nJ), leaving most stored energy unutilized.
motivation: Miniaturized energy-harvesting and battery-powered IoT devices require efficient burst-energy delivery for wireless transmission and peak computation without bulky external storage.
method: Capacitive power-management IC using single external storage capacitor charged to high voltage, continuously stepped up/down via on-chip switched-capacitor (SC) converter during burst mode, achieving 91.25% energy-extraction efficiency delivering up to 5.68mJ (40x improvement over prior on-chip approaches).
key_novelty: Single-capacitor high-voltage pre-charging strategy with on-chip step-up/-down SC converter enabling >35x burst-energy-delivery improvement vs. prior methods.
contributions: 146μJ burst energy from 22μF MLCC (35x improvement over 70%-efficient designs with similar footprint)
5.68mJ burst energy delivery from 220μF tantalum capacitor (40x vs. prior on-chip-only approach)
91.25% peak power-conversion efficiency without large on-chip capacitor arrays
limitations: Quiescent power consumption, charge/discharge cycle lifetime, and integration with specific IoT transceiver protocols not discussed.
primary_theme: Efficient burst-energy delivery via capacitive power management.
